prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Input image: edit target, the current B rhythm-game frame.
Primary request: redesign ONLY THE FOUR BUTTON MODULES in the bottom center. Maintain the exact composition, camera angle, perspective, row arrangement, module positions and overall footprint. Keep the entire outer frame, side gauges, lane area, lower bumper, background and all non-button artwork unchanged.

Make the button assembly feel like a refined tactile rhythm-game controller integrated with this silver and dark navy mechanical frame. Retain large broad flat rectangular striking surfaces. Give them clean chamfered corners, a restrained thin silver perimeter, a low-profile solid keycap and a clearly readable short-travel seam. Integrate the key and its lower emitter support with neat angular side cheeks and layered dark metal recesses. Rework the actual keycap, bevel, support and aperture design noticeably, not just its coloring.
The lower support should be a compact broad rectangular open mouth with clipped corners and a thin rim, rather than a hanging pointed tooth. Hollow its entire front face. ONE uninterrupted aperture per key. Keep the large key face dominant and the front opening visibly smaller than the key. No divider, twin hole, grille, circular light, arrows, icon, label or decorative round dial. The shape should be functional and uncluttered, matching the existing armor finish.

Keep the existing depicted states: ONLY the SECOND key from the left is physically pressed down and luminous pale cyan, with a WHITE-centered cyan flash in its single front aperture directed toward the viewer. Its travel should read clearly against the raised unlit charcoal keys 1, 3 and 4. The flash is a compact burst of light with a white core and cyan edge, not a flame or long jet. Preserve the open rim around the light. Do not let bloom obscure the new button design. Other three apertures are dark.
Same complete portrait frame and original composition. No cropping, no zoom, no separate panels, no text. Redesign only the button assembly in place.
